'''Ronald Jordan Hunter''' (born October 24, 1993) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and current assistant coach for the [[Tulane Green Wave]]. He played college basketball for the [[Georgia State Panthers men's basketball|Georgia State Panthers]] under the direction of his father and Georgia State head coach, [[Ron Hunter]], being named twice [[Sun Belt Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Sun Belt Player of the Year]] as well as the [[Sun Belt Conference]] Male Athlete of the Year. He holds the school record for most career points with a total of 1,819 after just three seasons of play.<ref name="GSU Player Bio">{{cite web|title=Player Bio: R. J. Hunter – Georgia State University Official Athletic Website|url=https://georgiastatesports.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/r-j-hunter/2318|work=[[Georgia State Panthers]]|publisher=[[Georgia State University]]|access-date=October 28, 2020}}</ref>

==High school career==
Hunter attended [[Pike High School]] in [[Indianapolis]] averaging 20.5 points, 6.6 rebounds, 3.8 assists and 2.9 steals per game as a senior. That year he led Pike to the Indiana State Championships, ending as a runner-up, and in the process earned All-Marion County First Team, a conference player of the year award and an Indiana All-Star mention.<ref name="GSU Player Bio"/>

==College career==
Hunter played three seasons for [[Georgia State University]] under his father and head coach, [[Ron Hunter]]. After his junior season, he declared for the [[2015 NBA draft]].

===Freshman season===
Hunter recorded a double-double with 14 points and 10 rebounds in his collegiate debut against No. 8 [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]]. He also scored 20 or more points 12 times during his freshman season, leading [[Georgia State Panthers men's basketball|GSU]] in scoring 15 times. He earned Kyle Macy Freshman All-America honors, [[Colonial Athletic Association|CAA]] Rookie of the Year, All-CAA First-Team and CAA All-Rookie Team after becoming the most prolific freshman scorer in Georgia State University history. Hunter finished the year with a school-record 527 points (17 PPG) and was one of just three freshmen in the country to average at least 17.0 points and 5.0 rebounds per game.<ref name="GSU Player Bio"/>

===Sophomore season===
[[File:R. J. Hunter 2014.jpg|thumb|left|Hunter in 2014]]
Hunter's trend of record setting continued into the rest of his career at GSU. Overall, he averaged 18.4 ppg, scoring 604 for the season and became the first Panther to make 100 3-pointers in a single season. That 3-pointer count was No. 16 in the [[NCAA]]. Hunter was excellent from the free-throw line, setting the school record in single-season average by hitting 88.2 percent (No. 1 percentage in the Sun Belt and No. 17 in the NCAA that season). As a part of that effort, he also set a school-record 38 straight free throws made. On defense, Hunter finished second in the Sun Belt and 49th in the NCAA with his 63 steals.

Many know Hunter from seeing highlights of his clutch buzzer-beater in the second round of the 2015 NCAA tournament, but hitting a shot like that was nothing new for him. In his sophomore year, Hunter scored a career-high 41 points against [[UTSA Roadrunners men's basketball|UTSA]], making a school single-game-record 12 three-pointers. The 12 threes were also the most in the country during the year and set a new [[Sun Belt Conference]] record. In another game that year, he hit the game-winning shot with 11.1 seconds to play against Arkansas State. Another clutch shot came in a game in which Hunter scored 31 points including a crucial 3-pointer with seven seconds left at [[UT Arlington Mavericks men's basketball|UT Arlington]] to send the game to overtime.<ref name="GSU Player Bio"/>

Hunter was named [[Sun Belt Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Sun Belt Conference Basketball Player of the Year]] as well as the Sun Belt Conference Male Athlete of the Year.<ref name=SUNBELT>{{cite news|url=http://sunbeltsports.org/news/2014/3/11/MBB_0311141240.aspx|title=Georgia State's Father-Son Duo Headlines Sun Belt Conference Men's Basketball Honorees|publisher=[[Sun Belt Conference]]|date=March 11, 2014|access-date=March 11, 2014}}</ref> He was also named the Men's Georgia College Player of the Year by the Atlanta Tipoff Club.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.georgiastatesports.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=12700&ATCLID=209432791|title=Hunter Earns Atlanta Tipoff Club Honor|publisher=[[Georgia State University]]|date=March 12, 2014|access-date=April 22, 2017}}</ref>

===Junior season===
In his final season at GSU, Hunter averaged a career-high 19.7 points, scoring a school-record season total of 688 points (a school record he broke each season). He also averaged 4.7 rebounds and 3.6 assists per game. In addition, he made 202 free-throws (No. 7 in the NCAA that year), second-most in school history, while swiping 75 steals, third-most in a single season in program history. The most noteworthy record he set was total career points. Midway through just his third season, Hunter overtook [[Rodney Hamilton]]'s record of 1,515 points with a basket in front of a GSU home crowd against [[Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns men's basketball|UL Lafayette]] on January 24, 2015. Hunter finished the year with a career total of 1,819 points.

The Panthers finished the 2014–15 season as the Sun Belt Conference regular season and tournament champions. With their Sun Belt Tournament championship win over [[Georgia Southern Eagles men's basketball|Georgia Southern]], the Panthers received a bid to the [[2015 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]]. In the round of 64, No. 14 seed Georgia State trailed the No. 3 seed [[2014–15 Baylor Bears basketball team|Baylor]] by 12 points with just 2:53 to play. Hunter took over and scored 12 of the Panthers' final 13 points, including a 30-foot 3-pointer with 2.6 seconds remaining to secure their electrifying come-from-behind upset win, which caused his coach (and father) Ron to fall off his stool in jubilation. The moment was selected as No. 2 in the NCAA's top 10 moments of the tournament, was included in the "[[One Shining Moment]]" montage following the championship game,<ref name="GSU Player Bio"/><ref name=dagger>{{cite news|first=Sam|last=Cooper|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/ncaab-the-dagger/dramatic-r-j--hunter-3-pointer-gives-georgia-state-upset-over-baylor--video-201128471.html|title=Dramatic R. J. Hunter 3-pointer gives Georgia State upset over Baylor (Video)|work=Yahoo Sports|date=March 19, 2015|access-date=March 19, 2015}}</ref> and was one of three nominees for the 2015 [[Best Upset ESPY Award]].<ref name=ESPYS>{{cite web|title=Best Upset Award Voting|url=http://www.espn.com/espys/2015/?voting=bestupset|website=[[ESPN]]|access-date=June 25, 2015}}</ref>

Hunter was again named both Sun Belt Conference Basketball Player of the Year and the Sun Belt Conference Male Athlete of the Year.<ref name="SUNBELT"/> R.J. was also the only player from a school in Georgia to be named to the Naismith Trophy watch list that season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/college/hunter-makes-naismith-trophy-list/oxC3n1GFdKX4NtJsmMfUJK/|title=R.J. Hunter makes Naismith Trophy list|newspaper=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]|date=December 3, 2014|access-date=October 28, 2020}}</ref>

===College records===
* All-time Georgia State University leader in points (1,819)
* All-time Georgia State University leader in free throws made (448), in free-throw percentage (.853), and in consecutive free throws made (38)
* All-time Georgia State University leader in 3-pointers made (253)
* Single-season Georgia State University leader in 3-pointers made (100, 2013–14)
* Single-season Georgia State University leader free-throw percentage (.882, 2013–14)
* Single-game Sun Belt Conference leader in 3-pointers made (12)
* Single-game Sun Belt Conference leader in free-throw percentage (1.000 16–16, 2015)

==Professional career==
===Boston Celtics (2015–2016)===
On June 25, 2015, Hunter was selected with the 28th overall pick in the [[2015 NBA draft]] by the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-select-rozier-hunter-mickey-and-thornton-2015-draft|title=Celtics Select Rozier, Hunter, Mickey and Thornton in 2015 Draft|work=NBA.com|date=June 26, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2020}}</ref> On July 27, he signed his rookie-scale contract with the Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-2015-first-round-draft-picks-terry-rozier-and-r.j.-hunter|title=Celtics Sign 2015 First Round Draft Picks Terry Rozier and R.J. Hunter|work=NBA.com|date=July 27, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2020}}</ref> After averaging just 2.8 points per game over his first eight NBA games, Hunter scored 12 points on 5-of-6 shooting off the bench against the [[Atlanta Hawks]] on November 24.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/game?gameId=400828097 |title=Celtics vs. Hawks - Game Summary - November 24, 2015|work=ESPN.com|date=November 24, 2015|access-date=October 28, 2020}}</ref> During his rookie season, Hunter received multiple assignments to the [[Maine Red Claws]], the Celtics' [[NBA G League|Development League]] affiliate.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 5, 2016|archive-date=March 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170322122733/http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|url-status=dead}}</ref> On October 24, 2016, Hunter was waived by the Celtics.<ref>{{cite web|first=Taylor C.|last=Snow|url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/sidebar/prac-102416-james-young-earns-celtics-final-roster-spot|title=James Young Earns Celtics' Final Roster Spot|work=NBA.com|date=October 24, 2016|access-date=October 26, 2016|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161108113651/http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/sidebar/prac-102416-james-young-earns-celtics-final-roster-spot|archive-date=November 8, 2016}}</ref>

===Chicago Bulls (2016)===
On October 27, 2016, Hunter signed with the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/release/bulls-sign-rj-hunter|title=BULLS SIGN R.J. HUNTER|work=NBA.com|date=October 27, 2016|access-date=October 28, 2020}}</ref> He was waived by the Bulls on December 29, 2016, after appearing in three games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/bulls/news/bulls-waive-rj-hunter|title=BULLS WAIVE RJ HUNTER|work=NBA.com|date=December 29, 2016|access-date=October 28, 2020}}</ref> During his time with Chicago, he had multiple assignments to the [[Windy City Bulls]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2016-17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=December 7, 2016|archive-date=January 26, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Long Island Nets (2017)===
On January 6, 2017, Hunter was acquired by the [[Long Island Nets]] of the NBA G-League.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://longisland.gleague.nba.com/news/long-island-nets-acquire-r-j-hunter|title=Long Island Nets Acquire R.J. Hunter|work=NBA.com|date=January 6, 2017|access-date=October 28, 2020}}</ref> Four days later, he made his debut for Long Island in a 120–112 loss to the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]], recording 22 points, three assists and two steals in 25 minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/games/20170110fwnlin|title=Alex Poythress' 28 Points Lift Mad Ants Over RJ Hunter, Nets|work=NBA.com|date=January 10, 2017|access-date=October 28, 2020}}</ref>

===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2017–2018)===
After failing to find a team to participate in training camp under the preseason, he would be assigned to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the D-League on October 24, 2017. Hunter made his debut with the team on November 4.

===Erie BayHawks (2018–2019)===
On January 14, 2018, Hunter signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Houston Rockets]]. On August 18, 2018, Hunter was waived by the Rockets.<ref>{{cite web|title=ROSTER UPDATE: Houston Rockets General Manager Daryl Morey announced today that the team has waived guard R.J. Hunter.|url=https://twitter.com/HoustonRockets/status/1030832077619560449|website=Houston Rockets on Twitter|access-date=August 18, 2018|date=August 18, 2018}}</ref>

On September 7, 2018, Hunter signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign R.J. Hunter|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/atlanta-hawks-sign-rj-hunter|website=NBA.com|access-date=September 7, 2018|date=September 7, 2018}}</ref> On October 13, 2018, Hunter was waived by the Hawks.<ref name="Hawks-camp-cuts">{{cite web|title=Hawks Request Waivers on Anderson, Hunter and Robinson|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-request-waivers-anderson-hunter-and-robinson|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 13, 2018|date=October 13, 2018}}</ref> Hunter was added to the training camp roster of the [[Erie BayHawks (2017–)|Erie BayHawks]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Hartman |first1=Billy |title=Erie BayHawks Finalize 2018 Training Camp Roster |url=https://erie.gleague.nba.com/news/erie-bayhawks-finalize-2018-training-camp-roster |website=NBA.com |access-date=October 28, 2020 |date=October 20, 2018}}</ref> In his BayHawks debut, Hunter scored a game-high 34 points on 12-of-18 shooting in a win over the [[Grand Rapids Drive]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Fernandes |first1=Victor |title=Hunter, BayHawks race past Drive in opener |url=https://www.goerie.com/sports/20181102/hunter-bayhawks-race-past-drive-in-opener |access-date=October 28, 2020 |work=[[Erie Times-News]] |date=November 2, 2018}}</ref>

===Return to Boston (2019)===
On January 10, 2019, Hunter signed a two-way contract with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Celtics Sign R.J. Hunter To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-rj-hunter-two-way-contract|access-date=January 30, 2022|website=NBA}}</ref>

===Türk Telekom (2019–2020)===
On June 27, 2019, Hunter signed with [[Türk Telekom B.K.|Türk Telekom]] of the Turkish [[Basketball Super League]] (BSL).<ref>{{cite web |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/rj-hunter-says-he-signed-with-turk-telekom-ankara/ |title=RJ Hunter says he signed with Turk Telekom Ankara |website=Sportando.com |access-date=June 27, 2019 |archive-date=October 30, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231030163120/https://sportando.basketball/en/rj-hunter-says-he-signed-with-turk-telekom-ankara/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===College Park Skyhawks (2020)===
On February 7, 2020, Hunter signed with [[College Park Skyhawks]] of the [[NBA G League]] (formerly D-League) and an affiliate of the [[Atlanta Hawks]] of the [[NBA]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.11alive.com/article/sports/basketball/college-park-skyhawks-introduce-rj-hunter-as-newest-player/85-37babf27-b130-4591-a293-5e8038ca3ada/ |title=College Park Skyhawks introduce former Georgia State hooper RJ Hunter as newest player |website=11alive.com |access-date=February 7, 2020}}</ref> He missed a game against the [[Greensboro Swarm]] on February 28 with an illness.<ref>{{cite news |title=R.J. Hunter: Misses Saturday's game |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/r-j-hunter-misses-saturdays-game/ |access-date=June 21, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 29, 2020}}</ref>

===Galatasaray (2020–2021)===
On July 21, 2020, Hunter signed with [[Galatasaray S.K. (men's basketball)|Galatasaray]] of the Turkish [[Basketball Super League|BSL]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Turkey/news/637100/Galatasaray-signs-R.J.-Hunter|title=Galatasaray signs R.J. Hunter|date=July 21, 2020|publisher=Eurobasket|language=En|access-date=July 22, 2020}}</ref>

===Sydney Kings (2021–2022)===
On July 23, 2021, Hunter signed with the [[Sydney Kings]] of the Australian [[National Basketball League (Australia)|NBL]] for the [[2021–22 NBL season|2021–22 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=RJ Hunter joins the Kings|url=https://www.sydneykings.com/news/rj-hunter-joins-the-kings|website=SydneyKings.com|date=July 23, 2021|access-date=July 23, 2021}}</ref> On January 15, 2022, he was ruled out for the rest of the season after rupturing his left patellar tendon.<ref>{{cite web|title=RJ Hunter to Miss Remainder of Season|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/rj-hunter-to-miss-remainder-of-season|website=NBL.com.au|date=January 15, 2022|access-date=January 15, 2022}}</ref> He was replaced on the roster.<ref>{{cite web|first=Brad|last=Winter|title=Here come the Kings: Sydney look like NBL title contenders once more|url=https://pickandroll.com.au/p/here-come-the-kings-sydney-look-like?s=r|website=PickAndRoll.com.au|date=February 1, 2022|access-date=May 9, 2022}}</ref>

===Greensboro Swarm (2023–2024)===
On September 29, 2023, Hunter signed with the [[Charlotte Hornets]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Hornets Sign R.J. Hunter And Edmond Sumner|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-sign-r-j-hunter-and-edmond-sumner|website=NBA.com|date=September 29, 2023|access-date=September 29, 2023}}</ref> but was waived on October 21, prior to the start of the [[2023–24 NBA season|2023–24 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Hornets Waive Brown, Hunter, Mensah|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/hornets-waive-brown-hunter-mensah|website=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 24, 2023}}</ref> Eight days later, he signed with the [[Greensboro Swarm]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Greensboro Swarm Announce Training Camp Roster and Coaching Staff for 2023-24 Season|url=https://greensboro.gleague.nba.com/news/greensboro-swarm-announce-training-camp-roster-and-coaching-staff-for-2023-24-season|website=NBA.com|date=October 29, 2023|access-date=November 5, 2023}}</ref>

On October 15, 2024, Hunter retired from professional basketball.<ref>{{cite Instagram|user=gtvhoops|title=Happy retirement to RJ Hunter! After nearly a decade long pro career, the former G League star has decided to hang it up at age 30. Hunter was the 28th pick in the 2015 NBA Draft by the Celtics and also had stints with the Bulls and Rockets. He spent a large part of his career in the G and posted career averages of 17.5 PPG, 3.7 RPG, and 3.3 APG with seven G League teams. Hunter averaged 20.4 PPG in 2018 with the Vipers and then 22.0 PPG the next year with the Skyhawks. He ranks 8th all-time in G League history in three-pointers and 27th in scoring. Congrats on a great career, @hunter_games31!|postid=DBKzQMNsugP|date=October 15, 2024|access-date=October 16, 2024}}</ref>

==Coaching career==
===Tulane (2024–present)===
In October 2024, Hunter joined his father on the coaching staff at [[Tulane Green Wave men's basketball|Tulane]] as a volunteer assistant coach.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tulane Men's Basketball Adds RJ Hunter to Coaching Staff |url=https://tulanegreenwave.com/news/2024/10/18/mens-basketball-tulane-mens-basketball-adds-rj-hunter-to-coaching-staff.aspx |access-date=2025-01-09 |website=Tulane University Athletics |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Hunter is the son of [[Ron Hunter]] and Amy Hunter, the youngest of two children. He and his older sister, Jasmine, are very close.<ref name="Ready for the NBA">{{cite web|first=Chris|last=Dortch|url=http://www.nba.com/2015/news/features/chris_dortch/02/26/draft-profile-on-georgia-states-r-j-hunter/|title=Georgia State's Hunter could be ready for jump to NBA|work=NBA.com|date=February 26, 2015|access-date=May 28, 2015}}</ref> Hunter's godfather is 15-year NBA veteran [[Ron Harper]].<ref name="GSU Player Bio"/>
